chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about hastening the Fitra by one day, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.' I said, 'So what do you think if we gather it and make its price silver and give it to one Muslim man?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Fitra (obligatory charity paid at the end of Ramadan)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay Fitra early and in cash/silver?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the jurisprudential flexibility (rukhsah) in administering Fitra, specifically permitting early payment and the conversion of the obligatory wheat or barley into a monetary equivalent (thaman) paid to a single recipient. This supports the Shia scholarly view that the form of Fitra is not strictly limited to specific foodstuffs, allowing for practical adaptation to local economic conditions while maintaining the core obligation of purifying the fasting person.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the hastening the Fitra by one day. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it'. I said, ‘So what is your<sup>asws</sup> view if we were to gather it and we make its price into silver and we give it to one Muslim man?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about paying al-Fitrah one day earlier. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’ I then asked, ‘Is it permissible to collect al-Fitrah and then turn it into waraq (cash) and give it to one Muslim person?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’”
